name: chicken
desc: Compiler for the Scheme programming language
why: A Scheme compiler that emits C, a strange and capable language ecosystem with a dedicated following and real depth.

brief.what_it_is: CHICKEN is a compiler for the Scheme programming language. It takes Scheme source files and produces portable, efficient C, which is then built into a native executable. It supports the R5RS and R7RS standards plus many extensions, and runs on Linux, OS X, Windows, and many Unix flavours. The package also ships an interpreter, csi, for running scripts directly.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no explicit motivation beyond describing CHICKEN as a Scheme compiler that is free, simple, portable, extensible, well documented, and actively supported.
brief.how_it_works: Source goes through csc, which emits C and compiles it into a binary, or through csi, which runs the script interpreted. The homepage's example shows both paths on a one-line hello-world program. Libraries, called eggs, are available through Eggs Unlimited and can be created by users.

commands_seen.context: Runs the homepage's hello-world.scm script interpreted with csi. The homepage shows it preceded by a $ shell prompt, which is not part of the command.
Compiles hello-world.scm into an executable binary with csc. The homepage shows it preceded by a $ shell prompt.
Runs the executable binary produced by csc. The homepage shows it preceded by a $ shell prompt.

brief.install_notes: The homepage lists the dependencies as a C toolchain and GNU Make, and calls installation easy. Eggs are fetched and installed with the chicken-install executable, which the brew formula also provides. The homepage does not describe first-run configuration or account setup.
brief.standout: It compiles Scheme to portable C and offers both an interpreter (csi) and a compiler (csc) from the same toolchain. The R5RS and R7RS support and the Eggs library ecosystem are also distinctive for a small, BSD-licensed Scheme.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage shows no release version, release date, or commit activity. The homepage says the project is actively supported, with mailing lists and an IRC channel (#chicken on Libera.Chat), but that is the project's own claim, not dated evidence.
brief.caveats: The homepage text is cut off mid-sentence at 'aims to be...', so its full claims are not visible. Building requires a C toolchain and GNU Make. The homepage names Linux, OS X, Windows, and many Unix flavours, but does not give details on Windows support. The brew caveats field is empty. The scout note calls the ecosystem 'strange', which is an editorial impression, not something the homepage says.
quotes: CHICKEN is a compiler for the Scheme programming language. It produces portable and efficient C and supports the R5RS and R7RS standards, and many extensions.
Distributed free for use and modification under the BSD License (freedom to user and developer).
Lightweight on dependencies (a C toolchain and GNU Make) and easy to install.
